nodes.rationale: FR-001 is complete at the prepared-source boundary: freshness measured exactly four merged engine commits after 0.67.0, including #2772 commit 7cef7301, zero Protocol.fs commits, and no unmerged bytes; the version, coherent-set, focused ReviewWait 19/19, ReviewApplication 7/7, local pack/install, and stale-token inversion checks passed. Those are direct worker/hosted checks plus the limited ReviewWait TRX, not one digest-tracked run that proves the whole inventory-and-SemVer subject, so this declaration does not mislabel that TRX as complete observed evidence.

FR-002 cannot execute before this prepared source merges: tags must identify the immutable merge and the release saga must then publish the once-packed payloads to both feeds before promotion. No tag, feed, or manifest success is claimed by the ReviewWait TRX.

FR-003 requires an independently downloaded public 0.68.0 tool. The local source-pack install reports 0.68.0.0 and focused source tests pass, but it is deliberately not substituted for nuget.org consumption or the installed #2797 route.

FR-004 is intentionally unfinished: registry/dependencies.yml and compatibility projections may only move from promoted release facts, the prepared changelog still says publication is owed, and freshness correctly reports four unreleased commits.

DEC-001's 0.68.0 classification is directly supported by freshness, version/coherent-set gates, and the release-note mismatch inversion, but those checks do not emit one durable observed-run receipt for this decision.

DEC-002's prepared-source boundary is satisfied through the current frozen PR and includes merged #2772 commit 7cef7301 while excluding unmerged work, but its immutable merge/tag half necessarily remains after merge.
DEC-003 is an unexecuted release transaction by design. The prepared source names release-saga/1, but no prepare/tag/publisher/promotion event is claimed before the source merge exists.

DEC-004 identifies manifest/journal/feed/install facts as acceptance authority; none exist for 0.68.0 yet. Hosted source CI and a local source-pack install are diagnostics, not substitutes for those future immutable facts.

DEC-005's source behavior preflight passed (ReviewWait 19/19, ReviewApplication 7/7, and hosted #2797 E2E 166/166), but the decision explicitly requires the installed public 0.68.0 tool; that final leg is outstanding.

PC-001's three projects evaluate to 0.68.0 and release-note/version gates pass, but those direct checks are not the ReviewWait TRX previously attached here. Publication must still prove that the package contract's served bytes use this scalar.

VO-001 intentionally spans pre-merge and post-merge gates. Its pre-merge release/version/focused-test/pack/install/inversion checks passed, while promotion, both-feed identity, public install, registry gates, and clear freshness remain unexecuted.

PM-001 is a documented additive migration posture rather than a test-run subject. S.I.R. remains deliberately blocked on the future 0.68.0 public install, so no receiver migration is claimed complete.

GV-001 is a generated-view currency subject, not ReviewWait behavior. The SDD generator establishes current pre-merge readiness views; final registry projections cannot be generated until promoted release facts exist.
